quandoUsar: Any single action on a page, form, or dialog: save, continue, cancel.
Actions whose label changes in place, like “Save” becoming “Saved”: the width follows the new text with a spring, with no jump.
Short async work where a loading indicator on the button itself is enough feedback (`loading` prop).
quandoEvitar: Use `action-button` when the button needs to show the pending and done states by itself after an async action.
Use `split-button` when the main action has close alternatives in a menu.
Use `hold-to-confirm` for destructive actions that need more than a click.

teclado.acao: Trigger the button; with `loading`, the activation is ignored.
Moves focus to the next control; the focus ring only appears with the keyboard (`:focus-visible`, a `foundation.css` rule).

acessibilidade: It is a native `<button>`: role, focus, and keyboard activation come from the browser.
During `loading` the button gets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, stays focusable, and keeps the label in the DOM for screen readers.
On an icon-only button, pass `aria-label` with the action name.
movimento: The press slightly reduces the button scale; anchors of menus and popovers do not scale, so the panel measures the right size.
When the content changes, the width animates with a spring with no overshoot and the label swaps with a short fade.
With “reduce motion”, the press scale and the width spring are turned off, the label swaps with a 0.12 s fade, and the loading indicator does not spin.
responsivo: The label does not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`); on narrow screens prefer short labels or the `sm` size.
Minimum heights come from the `--control-height-sm`, `-md`, and `-lg` tokens, so they follow the rest of the controls.
desempenho: Measuring the label width uses one observer per button; it is cheap, but avoid hundreds of them in a long list.
notasIA: Default choice for a single action; for a row of actions with icons prefer `floating-button-group` or `button-group`, and with close alternatives, `split-button`.
Pass the changing label (Save → Saved) as the child to get the width animation with no configuration; `loading` blocks `onClick` without disabling the button.

Variants `primary` (default), `secondary`, `ghost`, and `danger`, sizes `sm`, `md`, and `lg`; the component does not set `type`, so inside a `<form>` pass `type="button"` when the action does not submit.
